paragraphs: Friend, here's what gets me about this one. Paul hears the warning in Tyre. He hears it again from Agabus in Caesarea, and Agabus says it's what "the Holy Spirit says" (Acts 21:11). Then Paul answers, "I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus" (Acts 21:13). The warnings were never the problem. Paul knew what was ahead, and he went anyway, because the name of Jesus mattered more to him than his own comfort.

Now look at the people around him, because they teach something too. They love Paul. They plead with him, they weep, and they mean every word. But when he won't be talked out of it, they quiet down and say, "The Lord's will be done" (Acts 21:14). Friend, that is HARD. Loving someone sometimes means you stop pulling on their sleeve and trust God with them, and I would have been wrapped around that man's ankle the whole way to Jerusalem.

So what do we do with this, baker? Some things God asks of us will cost something, and He doesn't hide that from us. Be ready like Paul, and pray like his friends. Hold on to Jesus tighter than you hold on to your own plans. And the story isn't over, because Paul is walking into Jerusalem right now.
